regime: Risk-On Relief Bounce, Oil Spike Unwinds
summary: Yesterday's oil shock unwound today and risk came back. Crude reversed hard, down 3.79 percent to exactly 100.00, giving back a big chunk of Thursday's spike and flipping below its stop. That took the pressure off stocks. NQ bounced 0.86 percent to 29,393 and ES 0.77 percent to 7,661, both reclaiming the falling stops they lost yesterday and flipping their short term trend back up. Gold rose 0.72 percent to 4,390 but faded from a 4,445 high, so its bounce is tentative. VIX dropped about 11 percent to 15.84. August CPI printed this morning and the tape took it in stride, with the oil reversal doing most of the work.
psychology: Two days, two opposite tapes. Yesterday everything sold on the oil spike. Today it all reversed. If you traded both days with the same size and the same conviction, you probably got whipsawed. That is the lesson of a shock and reversal week: the market is not handing you a trend, it is handing you noise that looks like one. The traders who did well this week were not the ones who called the direction. They were the ones who cut size when the range doubled and waited for the tape to settle. A calmer VIX and stocks back above their stops is a better backdrop than yesterday, but two wild sessions in a row is a reason to stay measured, not to press. Let the market prove the bounce holds.

event.name: August CPI (release value not captured this run)
event.actual: August CPI was the scheduled release this morning. The market's reaction was risk on: stocks rallied, crude fell, and VIX dropped, so the print did not add fresh inflation fear to the tape. The exact CPI figure was not captured this run, so the read here is the price reaction, not the release value. The bigger mover was oil reversing. Crude gave back 3.79 percent to 100.00 after Thursday's supply shock spike, which eased both the inflation and growth worries that hit stocks yesterday.
event.surprise: Reaction was risk on: stocks up, crude down, VIX down, so the print did not add fresh inflation fear.
event.nqReaction: NQ bounced 0.86 percent to 29,393, reclaimed its falling stop, broke the opening range up to 29,499, then faded back into the range to close mid range.
event.crossAsset: Gold, which fell with stocks yesterday, bounced today but faded from its highs. VIX collapsed about 11 percent to 15.84.

risk.sizing: Volatility came in today and stocks are back above their stops, a calmer backdrop than yesterday. But this is the second wild session in a row and the Fed meets next week, so this is not the time to size up. Keep index size sensible and let the bounce prove itself.
risk.openRisk: For the indices the flipped up stops are the line. MNQ holding above 29,250 or MES above 7,640 on two hourly closes keeps the bounce intact. Below those, the short term trend flips back down. Upside references are the 29,500 zone on NQ and 7,681 then 7,700 on ES. December gold is back above its 4,383 stop but barely, so 4,383 is the pivot, with 4,400 and 4,445 above and 4,333 below. Crude flipped down, so it is now a with trend short below the 101.68 stop toward 98.77 then the 97s, and reclaiming 101.68 is the first repair.
risk.note: The Fed decides on rates Wednesday September 16 with fresh projections, so this was the last calm session before the market starts positioning for that. Prop accounts should note news blackout rules around the CPI release today and the Fed decision next week. Rising event risk into the FOMC decision Wednesday September 16 with fresh projections. Keep size sensible and mind prop news blackout rules around today's CPI print and the Fed next week. Not financial advice.

fullReport.title: NY Opening Range / HTA OPEN
fullReport.html: NQ printed a 93 point opening range: high 29,440, low 29,347. Price broke up out of the range at the open and tagged 29,499, then faded back below NYVWAP 29,432 and closed 29,393, back inside the range. In plain terms the upside break did not fully hold and price came back into the range, but the day still closed well above yesterday. For Monday the opening range resets fresh. BIR is blocked because Monday is a BIR skip day. HOF, MID, and BNC are eligible on the calendar, subject to their time windows.

fullReport.title: Momentum Breakout (Regime Filter)
fullReport.html: E3v2 Momentum Long looks more alive than it has all week. NQ and ES both closed back above their trend stops, so the index momentum filter is close to arming again after being off during the selloff. A fresh 15 minute breakout long is on the table if price holds above the flipped up stops. Crude is the opposite, a fresh short below a falling stop, so no long there. One bounce day after a shock is a spot to want confirmation before pressing a new long.

fullReport.title: AVWAP Deviation Band Reversal
fullReport.html: AVWAP deviation band (MNQ): AVWAP center 29,421, close 29,393 is about 1 sigma below the mean. Bands: plus 2 sigma 29,474, plus 1 sigma 29,447, minus 1 sigma 29,394, minus 2 sigma 29,368, minus 3 sigma 29,341. Sigma narrowed to about 27 today from yesterday's 33 as the tape calmed. Volume is unavailable on the continuous contract, so this is price only. The close sits right at the minus 1 sigma band, not stretched, so there is no clean reversion signal here. The band is a map for Monday: a push to plus 2 sigma near 29,474 or a flush to minus 2 sigma near 29,368 are the spots this edge looks to fade, best after price stops trending.
